title: SYSK’s 2021 Glad Tidings Bonanza Holiday Special
summary: Holiday special of Stuff You Should Know covering four Christmas topics plus a Festivus segment. The hosts open with the authorship dispute over "A Visit from St. Nicholas" ("'Twas the Night Before Christmas"), weighing Clement Clark Moore against the Livingston family and the Dutch origins of the reindeer names. Next is the origin of red and green as Christmas colors, including Christian symbolism, medieval miracle plays, Saturnalia, Celtic holly, church rood screens, and Thomas Nast's Santa. Then they cover the 1980s sitcom ALF's two-part Christmas episode, in which a dying girl, Tiffany, inspired the storyline. Next is the business of Christmas songs, including Slade's "Merry Xmas Everybody," Mariah Carey, and Last Christmas. Then the history of Advent calendars, from Gerhard Lang's 1908 version through the Nazi-era editions and Eisenhower's popularity in the US. The episode closes with Festivus, the Seinfeld holiday, and the real O'Keefe family tradition started by Daniel O'Keeffe Sr. The hosts end with thanks to listeners and staff.

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open the holiday special, noting it is ad-free and introducing the episode's Christmas topics.

segments.title: Authorship of 'Twas the Night Before Christmas
segments.summary: The hosts review the disputed authorship of 'A Visit from St. Nicholas.' It first appeared in the Troy Sentinel in 1823 without credit, and Clement Clark Moore was later named as author. Henry Livingston Jr.'s family claims he read it to his children years earlier and mentions a lost handwritten draft. They discuss the Dutch names of the reindeer and the anapestic meter, and note a statistical analysis from a New Zealand professor.

segments.title: Interstitial music
segments.summary: Jerry's Christmas interstitial music plays between segments.

segments.title: Origins of red and green Christmas colors
segments.summary: Theories for the red and green colors: Christian symbolism of evergreen and the blood of Christ, the Paradise Play with apples on a pine tree, Saturnalia, Celtic holly, red and green church rood screens, Victorian color schemes, and Haddon Sundblom's Coca-Cola Santa.

segments.title: Transition to ALF segment
segments.summary: Chuck picks the next topic and the hosts move on to the ALF Christmas episode.

segments.title: ALF Christmas special and Tiffany
segments.summary: The hosts describe the ALF sitcom and its two-part Christmas episode, in which Alf spends time with a dying girl named Tiffany. Yahoo's Ethan Adler discovered the episode's end card dedicated to a real girl, Tiffany Lee Smith, who had a video call with Alf through Make a Wish. The hosts discuss the episode's reception and the difficulty of finding part two.

segments.title: Christmas songs and royalties
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the money in Christmas songs, starting with Jim Lea of Slade, who wrote 'Merry Xmas Everybody' in a hotel bathroom in 1973. They mention Mariah Carey's 'All I Want for Christmas Is You,' Freddie Mercury, Queen, and Wham's 'Last Christmas,' and share favorite holiday songs and the Kmart intercom music video.

segments.title: Advent calendars
segments.summary: Advent calendars are described, with a brief history starting with Gerhard Lang's 1908 version. Nazi-era editions, the 1950s U.S. popularity boost via Eisenhower, and modern branded versions are touched on.

segments.title: Festivus
segments.summary: The Seinfeld holiday Festivus is discussed, with its origin in the episode 'The Strike' and the real O'Keefe family tradition, begun by Daniel O'Keeffe Sr. in 1966. Traditions include the airing of grievances, feats of strength, and the clock in the bag.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts thank listeners and staff, including the listener-suggestion contributors, and wish everyone happy holidays.
